Demo run review

Two AI characters → six themed gym slideshows → two CTA experiments, driven end-to-end through the ClipZoo UI. What worked, what fought back, and what to build next.

TL;DR — the flow works, and the output is genuinely postable. Paige and Bryce were created from attribute pickers plus a one-line description; their mirror-selfie "looks" (phone over face) came out identity-consistent and startlingly close to the reference photos. Six slideshows generated (3 themes each), all with an Evex CTA. Both CTA experiments succeeded technically, with a clear winner: the AI composite of a hand holding an iPhone showing the real app screenshot beats the raw screenshot, whose dense UI collides with overlaid CTA text. Two Bryce posts needed a regeneration pass (a look with too much face visible slipped into rotation) — the fix loop itself was fast, which is its own good sign. Main product gaps: no way to upload a reference image for a character, no one-click "add look to a collection", and no control over which hook image gets picked per generation.

The cast

Paige Female · 25-30 · athletic — for the female-audience posts. Bryce Male · 25-30 · athletic — for the male-audience posts. Portrait first (left), then reference-based looks. Every look was prompted as a mirror selfie with the iPhone covering the face — the current meta.

Paige: portrait, luxury-gym selfie, apartment selfie, golden-hour studio selfie. Identity holds across scenes.

Bryce: portrait, industrial-gym selfie, loft selfie (the motorcycle from the reference image made it in unprompted), and the garage-gym replacement look generated during QA.

The six slideshows

Each: hook slide from the character's look collection, four numbered content slides, CTA slide with an Evex plug. Outlined text style throughout. Titles and hashtag captions were AI-written per post.

Paige 1 — "how i actually got lean for summer (no crash diet)" PASS

Apartment mirror-selfie hook, coherent habit content, AI-generated feminine b-roll, composite CTA. No issues.

Paige 2 — "signs you are officially becoming that girl at the gym" PASS

Gym mirror-selfie hook. Slide texts land the playful tone ("your gym split is actually… fun?").

Paige 3 — "what i wish someone told me before my first gym session" PASS

Good content; two nits noted below — the hook reused the same apartment look as post 1, and the 3-line CTA text crowds the phone graphic slightly.

Bryce 1 — "how i finally saw gym results after 2 years of nothing" PASS after regen

First attempt used a locker-room look where the phone only half-covered the face — meta violated, so I pruned that look from the collection, generated a garage-gym replacement, and regenerated. Shown: final version.

Bryce 2 — "5 gym mistakes keeping you small" PASS after regen

Same fix as Bryce 1. The blunt tone works ("Leg day isn't optional. Build a base.").

Bryce 3 — "the boring routine that finally got me lean and strong" PASS

Loft/motorcycle hook. This one deliberately keeps the raw screenshot CTA as the preserved experiment B example — see below.

CTA experiments

How the flow held up

StepExperienceFriction
Character creationExcellent. Attribute chips + one "extra details" line got both references close on the first try. Portraits in ~3-5s.No way to upload a reference photo — the closest I could get to your reference images was describing them.
Looks generationExcellent. Identity held across all scenes; "phone covering face" prompts respected 6 of 7 times.One look showed too much face and there's no regenerate-in-place — delete and re-prompt.
Looks → collectionWorks, but only via manual re-upload.Looks live in Characters; collections can't see them. I had to move files by hand (via API). Needs an "add to collection" button on each look.
CTA reference imageThe composite result is a standout — reference-based generation reproduced real UI text.This flow doesn't exist in the UI. I created a throwaway character and swapped its portrait file on disk. Worth productizing as "generate image from a reference upload".
Automation configAll the pieces exist: per-slide image overrides, pinned specific images, collection hooks, fixed CTA position.CTA at "last" needs a fixed slide count for image overrides to target it reliably — position math is easy to get wrong silently.
Generation~45-52s with 4 AI content images; ~6-10s when content slides come from a collection. Viewer modal on completion is a good loop.Hook selection is random from the bank; theme control required editing topic+hooks between runs. A "generate with this hook" picker would remove the dance.
QA / fix loopFast: prune look → new look → regenerate took under 3 minutes end to end.Hook image is also random — same look appeared on 2 of 3 posts for each character. No per-generation pin.
Timings & cost notes
  • Character portrait: ~3-5s each (Gemini flash image). Looks: ~3-5s each. 10 look/portrait images total, including the QA replacement and the CTA composite.
  • Slideshow with 4 AI content slides (Paige): 44-52s. With collection content slides (Bryce): 6-10s. Collection-based content is effectively free and much faster — worth surfacing in the UI as a cost hint.
  • Total Gemini image spend for the whole demo: roughly 25 generated images (~a dollar-ish at flash-image rates); text generation negligible.
  • 8 slideshows generated in total to end at 6 keepers (2 regenerated during QA).
